requirements.title: core.Named picks tools by name
requirements.rationale: Every example filters a tool set by name with a switch or a map; one call with a precise error replaces that wiring.

criteria.condition: core.Named(ts, names...) is called and every entry of names occurs once in names and is the Name of a top-level tool in ts
criteria.action: return, for each entry of names in order, the first tool in ts whose Name equals that entry exactly, without searching any tool's ReachableTools
criteria.contract: ([]core.Tool with len(names) elements whose Names equal names in order, nil error)

setup: a set ts of tools read_file, write_file, list_files in that order
a wrapper tool in ts whose ReachableTools hold a tool named hidden
two tools in a second set both named dup, with different Descriptions
check.pseudocode: got, err = core.Named(ts, 'list_files', 'read_file'); assert err == nil; assert names(got) == ['list_files','read_file']; _, err = core.Named(ts, 'hidden'); assert err != nil; d, _ = core.Named(dupSet, 'dup'); assert d[0].Description == first.Description

criteria.action: return a newly allocated slice of value copies, leave ts and its elements unmodified, and not share ts's backing array, so that writing to a result element leaves ts unchanged
criteria.contract: ts[i].Description is unchanged for every i; appending to the result does not change ts; the result's backing array differs from ts's (&got[0] != &ts[idx])

setup: a set ts of three tools with distinct Descriptions
check.pseudocode: got,_ = Named(ts,'read_file'); got[0].Description='x'; assert ts[0].Description == orig; assert &got[0] != &ts[0]

criteria.condition: core.Named is called with no names
criteria.action: return an empty slice
criteria.contract: (non-nil []core.Tool of length 0, nil error)

setup: a non-empty tool set, and separately a nil tool set
check.pseudocode: got, err = Named(ts); assert got != nil && len(got)==0 && err == nil; got, err = Named(nil); assert got != nil && len(got)==0 && err == nil

criteria.condition: one or more entries of names are not the Name of any top-level tool in ts
criteria.action: return no tools and an error whose text begins "core: ", quotes every missing name in names order, and lists every Name in ts in ts order or states that the set is empty
criteria.contract: (nil, error) e.g. `core: no tool named "no_such_tool"; the set holds: read_file, write_file`

setup: a set ts of read_file and write_file in that order
an empty tool set
check.pseudocode: got, err = Named(ts,'no_such_tool'); assert got == nil; assert err.Error() == 'core: no tool named "no_such_tool"; the set holds: read_file, write_file'; assert index(err2,'"b_missing"') < index(err2,'"a_missing"')

criteria.condition: every entry of names is present in ts but at least one entry appears more than once in names
criteria.action: return no tools and an error whose text begins "core: " and quotes the first repeated name
criteria.contract: (nil, error) with the quoted first repeated name in its text

setup: a set ts holding read_file, write_file and list_files
check.pseudocode: got, err = Named(ts,'read_file','write_file','write_file','read_file'); assert got == nil; assert hasPrefix(err,'core: ') && contains(err,'"write_file"')

criteria.action: for any tool set ts and any sequence of distinct names drawn from ts's Names, return tools whose Names equal that sequence, and return identical results when called concurrently from multiple goroutines on the same ts (race detector reports nothing)
criteria.contract: the returned Names equal the requested sequence; every concurrent result equals the sequential result; the race detector reports nothing (go test -race)

setup: a generated tool set ts with distinct names
check.pseudocode: for ts, picks in gen(): got,_ = Named(ts,picks...); assert names(got)==picks; parallel(8): assert names(Named(ts,picks...))==picks

requirements.title: guard.Allow is Restricted with only AllowedPrograms
requirements.rationale: The allowlist guard is the common case and must be one call without opening a second code path or aliasing the caller's slice.

criteria.action: for any program list and any tool-call context, return a decision whose Block, Reason and Terminate equal those returned by guard.Restricted(guard.Options{AllowedPrograms: programs}) for the same context, so block reasons keep the "guard.Restricted: " prefix
criteria.contract: core.BeforeToolCall decision equal field-by-field to Restricted's

setup: guard.Restricted(Options{AllowedPrograms: programs}) as the oracle
check.pseudocode: a = Allow(progs...); r = Restricted(Options{AllowedPrograms: progs}); for ctx in gen(): da=a(ctx); dr=r(ctx); assert da == dr

criteria.condition: the caller modifies, appends to or reorders the slice it passed to guard.Allow after Allow has returned
criteria.action: keep making the decisions it made for the program list as it was when Allow was called
criteria.contract: a program added to the caller's slice after Allow returns stays blocked

setup: programs := []string{"ls", "cat"} with spare capacity
a guard built by Allow(programs...)
check.pseudocode: g = Allow(progs...); progs[1]='rm'; progs = append(progs,'curl'); assert g(exec('rm x')).Block; assert g(exec('curl u')).Block; assert !g(exec('ls')).Block; assert !g(exec('cat f')).Block

criteria.condition: guard.Allow is called with no programs
criteria.action: block every execute and run_command call and allow every call to any other tool
criteria.contract: Block=true for shell tools, Block=false for non-shell tools

setup: g := guard.Allow()
check.pseudocode: g=Allow(); assert g(ctx('execute','ls')).Block; assert g(ctx('run_command','ls')).Block; assert !g(ctx('read_file',...)).Block

requirements.title: faux.ToolCall and faux.Text build single-block turns
requirements.rationale: Offline examples script single-block turns with verbose literals; a helper per turn shape removes them without changing what the provider emits.

criteria.condition: faux.ToolCall(id, name, args) is called with args that is a JSON object
criteria.action: return a Turn whose Blocks hold exactly the block faux.FauxToolCall(id, name, args) returns, whose StopReason is core.StopReasonToolUse, and whose other fields are zero
criteria.contract: reflect.DeepEqual to faux.Turn{Blocks: []core.ContentBlock{faux.FauxToolCall(id, name, args)}, StopReason: core.StopReasonToolUse}

setup: id "c1", name "read_file", args `{"path":"a"}`
check.pseudocode: assert DeepEqual(faux.ToolCall(id,name,args), faux.Turn{Blocks: []core.ContentBlock{faux.FauxToolCall(id,name,args)}, StopReason: core.StopReasonToolUse})

criteria.condition: faux.Text(s) is called
criteria.action: return a Turn whose Blocks hold exactly core.TextBlock{Text: s}, whose StopReason is core.StopReasonStop, and whose other fields are zero
criteria.contract: reflect.DeepEqual to faux.Turn{Blocks: []core.ContentBlock{core.TextBlock{Text: s}}, StopReason: core.StopReasonStop}

setup: strings "", "hello" and a multi-line string
check.pseudocode: for s in cases: assert DeepEqual(faux.Text(s), faux.Turn{Blocks: []core.ContentBlock{core.TextBlock{Text: s}}, StopReason: core.StopReasonStop})

criteria.condition: faux.ToolCall is called with args that is empty or only whitespace
criteria.action: build the tool-use block with the input {}, as core.NewToolUse does
criteria.contract: the returned block's input is the JSON text {}

setup: args values "", "  " and "\n\t"
check.pseudocode: for a in ['',' ','\n\t']: b = faux.ToolCall('c','t',a).Blocks[0].(core.ToolUseBlock); assert string(b.Input)=='{}'

criteria.condition: faux.ToolCall is called with args that is not a JSON object
criteria.action: panic with a message that names faux.ToolCall, the id and the tool name
criteria.contract: panic value is a string containing "faux.ToolCall", the quoted id and the quoted name

setup: args values `[1]`, `"s"`, `12` and `{bad`
check.pseudocode: for a in bad: msg = recoverString(func(){faux.ToolCall('id7','my_tool',a)}); assert contains(msg,'faux.ToolCall') && contains(msg,'"id7"') && contains(msg,'"my_tool"')

criteria.condition: a faux.Provider is scripted with turns built by faux.ToolCall and faux.Text
criteria.action: emit exactly the event sequence it emits when scripted with the equivalent one-block Turn literals
criteria.contract: the collected core events are reflect.DeepEqual between the two scripts

setup: a real faux.Provider A scripted with faux.ToolCall(...) then faux.Text(...)
a real faux.Provider B scripted with the equivalent one-block Turn literals
check.pseudocode: evA = collect(faux.New(ToolCall(..),Text(..))) per call; evB = collect(faux.New(literal1, literal2)); assert DeepEqual(evA, evB)

requirements.title: sandbox.Open creates, fills and equips a sandbox in one call
requirements.rationale: Embedders repeat Create, Sync and Tools with separate error checks; one call in the order that satisfies GitRepo's slot rules removes the wiring.

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open(ctx, p, spec, src, opts) is called with a non-nil p and a non-nil src
criteria.action: call p.Create(ctx, spec), then Sync(ctx, src) on the new sandbox, then Tools(ctx, opts), each once and in that order, and discard the SyncResult
criteria.contract: (the Sandbox value Create returned, identical and not wrapped; the proxies Tools returned; nil error)

setup: a test double Provider and Sandbox in package sandbox_test that records calls and their contexts
a non-nil Source (LocalDir) and ToolOptions{SpillDir: "/abs"}
a ctx carrying a value
check.pseudocode: sb, tools, err = Open(ctx,p,spec,src,opts); assert p.calls==['Create','Sync','Tools']; assert sb == p.created; assert p.created.closeCalls == 0

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open is called with a nil src
criteria.action: call p.Create(ctx, spec) and then Tools(ctx, opts) without calling Sync
criteria.contract: (the Sandbox Create returned, the proxies Tools returned, nil error)

setup: a recording test double Provider and Sandbox
check.pseudocode: Open(ctx,p,spec,nil,opts); assert p.calls==['Create','Tools']

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open succeeds
criteria.action: return without calling Close on the sandbox and without retaining ctx, leaving the sandbox's lifetime to the caller
criteria.contract: the returned sandbox's Close has been called zero times

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open is called on the local provider with a sandbox.LocalDir source holding project files
criteria.action: return a live sandbox whose returned proxies have the same Names, in the same order, as a later Sandbox.Tools call with equal options, and whose read_file proxy reads a synced file's content; a later Sync, Export and Close on the sandbox succeed
criteria.contract: (live Sandbox, []core.Tool, nil error); the synced file's content is returned by read_file

setup: the local provider (local.Unisolated) with TMPDIR set to a temp dir (skipped on Windows)
a host directory with src/main.go containing known text
check.pseudocode: sb, tl, err = Open(...); assert err==nil; assert names(tl)==names(sb.Tools(ctx,ToolOptions{})); out = find(tl,'read_file').Execute(ctx,{path:'src/main.go'}); assert contains(out, text); assert sb.Sync(...)==nil; assert sb.Export(...)==nil; assert sb.Close(ctx)==nil

requirements.title: sandbox.Open fails cleanly
requirements.rationale: A failure after Create must not leak a sandbox, and the caller must still be able to match the step's error.

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open is called with a nil Provider
criteria.action: return an error without panicking and without calling anything
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, error whose text begins "sandbox: ")

setup: a nil sandbox.Provider interface value
check.pseudocode: sb,tl,err = Open(ctx,nil,spec,src,opts); assert sb==nil && tl==nil && hasPrefix(err.Error(),'sandbox: ')

criteria.condition: p.Create returns an error
criteria.action: return Create's error unchanged and call no Sandbox method
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, err) where err == Create's error

setup: a test double Provider whose Create returns a distinct error E
check.pseudocode: sb,tl,err = Open(...); assert err == E; assert p.sandboxCalls == 0

criteria.condition: Sync or Tools returns an error and the sandbox's Close then succeeds
criteria.action: call Close exactly once on the sandbox with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) and return the step error unchanged
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, err) where err == the step error; Close called once

setup: a test double whose Sync fails with error S in one case and whose Tools fails with error T in another
Close succeeds in both
check.pseudocode: for step in [Sync,Tools]: sb,tl,err = Open(...); assert sb==nil && tl==nil; assert err == stepErr; assert double.closeCalls == 1

criteria.condition: Sync or Tools returns an error and the sandbox's Close also returns an error
criteria.action: return errors.Join(stepErr, closeErr)
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, err) where errors.Is(err, stepErr) and errors.Is(err, closeErr) both hold

setup: a test double whose Sync (or Tools) fails with S and whose Close fails with C
check.pseudocode: sb,tl,err = Open(...); assert errors.Is(err,S) && errors.Is(err,C); assert closeCalls==1

criteria.condition: ctx is cancelled or past its deadline when Sync or Tools fails
criteria.action: still call Close, passing a context whose Err() is nil and whose values are those of ctx
criteria.contract: Close observes ctx.Err() == nil; the step error is returned

setup: a ctx with a value under a private key, then cancelled (also tested with an expired deadline)
a test double whose Sync fails and whose Close records ctx.Err() and ctx.Value(key)
check.pseudocode: ctx,cancel = WithCancel(WithValue(bg,k,'v')); cancel(); _,_,err = Open(ctx,...); assert double.closeErr == nil && double.closeVal=='v'; assert errors.Is(err, S)

criteria.action: for any failing step (Sync or Tools) and any sentinel X that the step error matches under errors.Is (including ErrUnsupported, ErrToolMismatch and ErrUnsafeArchive), return an error that also matches X under errors.Is, whether or not Close failed
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, err) with errors.Is(err, X) true for every X that errors.Is(stepErr, X) is true for

setup: a test double with a configurable failing step (Sync or Tools), a step error wrapping a sentinel, and a Close that succeeds or fails
check.pseudocode: for step,X,closeFails in gen(): stepErr = fmt.Errorf('ctx: %w',X); _,_,err = Open(...); assert errors.Is(err,X)

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open is called on the local provider with a sandbox.GitRepo source
criteria.action: close the sandbox and remove its directory under os.TempDir()/agentkit-sandbox-local/ before returning
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, err) with errors.Is(err, sandbox.ErrUnsupported); no entry remains under agentkit-sandbox-local

setup: the local provider with TMPDIR set to t.TempDir() (skipped on Windows)
check.pseudocode: _,_,err = Open(ctx, local, spec, GitRepo{URL:'x'}, ToolOptions{}); assert errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupported); assert entries(TMPDIR+'/agentkit-sandbox-local') == []

criteria.condition: sandbox.Open is called on the local provider with a relative ToolOptions.SpillDir
criteria.action: close the sandbox after Tools is refused and remove its directory under os.TempDir()/agentkit-sandbox-local/ before returning
criteria.contract: (nil, nil, err) whose text contains "sandbox: agent refused Tools"; no entry remains under agentkit-sandbox-local

setup: the local provider with TMPDIR set to t.TempDir() (skipped on Windows)
a host directory with one file
check.pseudocode: _,_,err = Open(..., ToolOptions{SpillDir:'rel'}); assert contains(err.Error(),'sandbox: agent refused Tools'); assert entries(root)==[]

requirements.rationale: The code a reader copies should show the scenario, not the wiring.

criteria.condition: the codemode example runs offline
criteria.action: print the same output as before the rewrite, so TS-08-49 passes unmodified
criteria.contract: stdout contains "Go files: main.go, util.go", "CHANGELOG.md: read_failed", `Return value: {"apples": 12, "pears": 0}` and "called inventory__stock"

setup: examples/codemode rewritten on core.Named, faux.ToolCall and faux.Text

execution_paths.title: An embedder builds a code-mode agent from named workspace tools and a scripted model

steps.action: opens a workspace with workspace.Open and builds its tools with tools.For(ws, tools.Options{})
returns list_files, find_files and read_file in that order
wraps them with codemode.New and scripts a faux.Provider with faux.ToolCall and faux.Text turns
runs with agentkit.Config{Toolset: agentkit.Toolset{…}} and executes the scripted code_mode calls against the workspace
prints the Go file list, the read_failed marker, the return value and the inventory__stock call

setup: the real examples/codemode main with its temp workspace and mocked inventory tool, offline
end_state: core.Named picks list_files, find_files, read_file in that order
the agent runs the faux.ToolCall/faux.Text script against the workspace
output includes the Go file list, the read_failed marker, the return value and the inventory__stock call

execution_paths.title: An embedder opens a local sandbox, runs a guarded agent in it and exports the result

steps.action: writes project files to a host directory and calls sandbox.Open(ctx, localProvider, spec, sandbox.LocalDir{Path: src}, sandbox.ToolOptions{})
creates the sandbox, syncs the directory into it and returns the sandbox with its proxy tools
picks read_file, search_files and execute with core.Named and sets guard.Allow("ls") as the guard
runs the faux.ToolCall/faux.Text script; the guard blocks rm with blocked_by_policy
exports src to a host directory and is closed by the deferred Close, removing its directory

setup: a host temp dir with project files and the local provider (skipped on Windows)

src is exported to a host directory containing main.go and util.go
the deferred Close removes the sandbox directory under agentkit-sandbox-local

closes the sandbox with context.WithoutCancel(ctx), removing its directory under agentkit-sandbox-local
receives (nil, nil, err) with errors.Is(err, sandbox.ErrUnsupported)
